name: KY-040 rotary encoder
senses: its knob being turned left or right and pressed
identification: Black PCB with a tall metal shaft on a square metal body and 5 angled header pins labelled CLK, DT, SW, + and GND.

confirmations.question: Read the 5 pin labels on the rotary encoder. Are they CLK, DT, SW, + and GND?
confirmations.reason: Clone modules differ. The wiring plan is only valid for a module with exactly these labels.

facts.statement: The module has five pins: the two rotation signals (CLK, DT), the button (SW), supply (+) and ground (GND).
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-040, pin drawing (vendor documentation for the Joy-IT module; clones may differ)

facts.statement: The vendor wires the module to 3.3 V on Raspberry Pi and to 5 V on a classic Arduino. No supply rating is published.

With each step of the knob CLK and DT change state one after the other. When CLK changes, the knob was turned one way if DT differs from CLK and the other way if they are equal. Powered from 3.3 V the signals cannot rise above 3.3 V.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-040, description and code example

facts.statement: Pressing the knob pulls SW LOW. The vendor's example switches on the board's internal pull-up resistors for all three signals; LearnLens sketches do not, so whether they read reliably is not confirmed.
